steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Wait a moment, Senior Executor. So you never intended to bring Arturia back to Landen Monastery?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I never stated that I would.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Well, if you won't, I will!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: There are certain things I must still ascertain with Arturia.
Now, now, Federico, it won't do to torment a poor nun like that.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Richele?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Did you have to run away so suddenly? All I did was joke around with you a little in front of that confessional.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What was the joke?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Uh, okay... anyway, I know this fugitive's a tough one, so I brought reinforcements.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Giving up my chance to witness the Nativity in the process. Aren't you touched?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I never requested assistance from the Notarial Hall.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I know, I know. You hardly ever work with the other executors.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You think I volunteered for this? Special orders, jointly issued by all seven tribunals of the Curia.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Pretty shocked when I got the orders... for a moment there, I thought Arturia had convinced you to commit treason.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have no such intention, and she has no such power.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have completed my assessment and determined that any risk to the Curia can be eliminated. You and your men may stand down now, Executor Richele.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Are you defying the special orders, Federico?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You have no authority to refuse.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: My orders were to oversee Federico's apprehension of Arturia before the Nativity, and to bring both of you in, should there be any suspicious behavior.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Not so fast, Senior Executor.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Were you talking to me, Seniora Arturia?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've been sitting in that monastery ever since I got back. I think I would like to stretch my legs for a while longer still.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's been more than a decade since I last saw night fall upon the Holy City... the view from this spot is remarkable.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: So you're resisting arrest... Oh, I do so hate overtime.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Stay behind us, Sister Hildegard.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You do the honors, Federico. You've been on this criminal's case for years. No one knows her tricks better than you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Looks like the Lateran has long had its eye on you, Fede.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Raise your gun. It won't be the first time.
Arturia stands at the edge of the roof. Federico has many questions, but he can see that her fingers are already touching the strings.
Behind her, Federico sees the Shrine of Nurtury, so tall he cannot see the top, and the infinite crowd meandering towards it.
Richele and his other colleagues stand behind him. Federico hears the sound of weapons being locked and loaded.
Tension runs high. It is as though he must prove something as executor.
There is no time to think. Federico raises his gun.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You have admitted to escaping confinement, Arturia. By the authority of the Lateran Notarial Hall, I am hereby reassessing your danger level and apprehension procedures.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You must fulfill your obligations as a Lateran citizen and work with us to resolve any threat to Laterano.
Without warning, the muzzle of Federico's gun flashes.
At the same time, music pours out of the cello, becoming one with the hymns emitting from the direction of the Shrine of Nurtury, drowning out the sounds on the roof.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ugh—!

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Federico! What are you doing?!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I shot at the building beside you. I did not strike any of you.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: But... that hurts... Mastigia! I think a rock hit my head... am I bleeding?

spans.text: I think a rock hit my head... am I bleeding?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Do you know what you've done, Federico...?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes, you are bleeding.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will submit a detailed report once the incident is resolved.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I will include a detailed explanation of the head injury you have suffered.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: That was decisive, Senior Executor.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Now, how do you intend to handle all these unconscious people... what are you looking for?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Richele has an annual pass for the confessionals. They can deliver these people to a hospital.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Now, share your discoveries and work with me to resolve any dangers to Laterano.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's just a guess.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You chased me all the way here, then got your cohorts out of the way. You've evidently arrived at the same theory I have.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It's almost time, Fede.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Perhaps the city itself will soon tell us exactly what has happened to it.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I've never seen so many outsiders in Laterano.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: That's for sure.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: The last Summit of Nations didn't have enough guests to fill a single hotel.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Just about every cardinal in the Curia is here... it's so crowded. The air is even more awkward than the Basilica.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: We're far enough on the edge, Mostima. We're like the cleaners standing against the wall of a casino.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Whatever this Nativity is, it's probably Andoain bringing out a Sankta kid who just learned to talk, so the Matriarch standing there gets to ceremonially polish the kid's halo...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: All symbolic puff. We could be home watching One-Armed Chainsaw Guy 2 instead.

spans.text: All symbolic puff. We could be home watching

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Let's just think of it as watching Nurturer Andoain work.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Haven't you already said all that needs to be said to him?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: My heart's been feeling twitchy for some reason...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Do you feel it, Mostima?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Yeah.
Fiammetta turns sideways. She has never seen such a serious expression on her friend's face.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I'm feeling nervous... no, anxious, fearful. It's excitement and expectation, and I don't know why...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I can't describe it. It's like my heartbeat isn't my own.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Is this empathy?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You're a fallen Angel and I'm a Liberi. Neither of us has the power. No, it's not just us...
Fiammetta scans the crowd, and is now certain that this heartbeat is not an illusion.
The emotions that she is feeling are written on every face in the crowd. Every heart present throbs to this beat, which does not belong to them.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: ...Look up.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Comfort bells.
Fiammetta follows her friend's gaze.
All the doors and windows were closed when the Nativity began. Not so much as a breeze can get in.

But the comfort bells are swaying in time, the ones hanging in the Hall of Enlightenment with them, and the ones in the corridors leading to the nurseries. Yet they do not produce the chimes that they should.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: A sort of medium... like the musical devices that Leithanians use.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: If my guess is right, we're feeling the heartbeat of the mother who is giving birth.

steps.name: Sankta
steps.text: It's exactly the same!

steps.name: Sankta
steps.text: It's exactly the same as what I felt when I waited outside the delivery room when my wife gave birth!

steps.name: Sankta
steps.text: I could feel the unfathomable pain, but she would not give up. Her emotions tugged at mine, and we both spoke the name that we had already decided...

steps.name: Sankta
steps.text: 'Bailey, Bailey...'

steps.name: Liberi
steps.text: Lord above!

steps.name: Liberi
steps.text: The mother fainted? She's too weak. The pain of birthing is more than she can take... i-it's not good!

steps.name: Perro
steps.text: My heart's about to leap out of my mouth.

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: She's not giving up...

steps.name: Liberi
steps.text: Lord, Holy City Most Pure, have mercy on us.

steps.name: Lupo & Kuranta & Feline
steps.text: Have mercy on us.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Have mercy on us.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: So... this really is a form of... 'empathy'.
Comfort bells sway violently throughout the hall. The ever-shifting emotions in the irregular heartbeats tug at everyone's nerves.
No one knows who the mother is, what her name is, how old she is, where she came from... but everyone knows what she is experiencing. No one moves a single step.

The fragile newborn has not yet triumphed over death. The struggle to break through the shell of ignorance seems eternal. Inside the Shrine of Nurtury, thousands of people experience a childbirth together—
Such clear empathy should never have existed in Laterano.
After a long, long time...
The heartbeat begins to weaken, until all is silent.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Connect the sensor wire, and activate the timer.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: The last bomb... is ready!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Dammit, it's really hard not to march to this heartbeat!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: *pant*—*pant*—

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Fortunately, I've got the quickest brain in Penguin Logistics!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I could play Super Music Tycoon with one hand and raygun bottle shooting with the other, and beat both the boss and Texas at the same time!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: All that practice wasn't for nothing!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Two minute countdown.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Blow up this corridor, and the path to the nursery will be cut off.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I hope my sister's intel is good...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: The Shrine of Nurtury took a pregnant Sarkaz from a nomadic abbey, and got her to give birth to a Sarkaz at the Summit of Nations in this crazy ceremony...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I don't know what they're trying to do, but if I can keep her from appearing in front of the crowd—
Excuse me, you're in the way.
The mother is about to give birth. I want to get closer and pray for her.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Sorry, I'll…

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Pregnant... Sarkaz... aren't you the one?!

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Yeah. What of it?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Shouldn't you be giving birth—

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Lemuel, right?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: We've met before. Your sister brought you to our place.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Oh, er, Fiammetta's grandpa... salve...

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: The others are searching for the bombs and neutralizing them, Reverend Patrizion.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Good work.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Stop this Sankta. She has more explosives on her.

steps.name: Shrine Patrol
steps.text: Snipers are in position. We will shoot to kill if the suspect attempts to escape.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Reverend Patrizion...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You're late, Cardinal Lemuen.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Take the suspect back to the Seventh Tribunal.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But if the Nativity isn't about this Sarkaz, then...?
The heartbeat that resonated throughout the hall has quieted down.
A door opens to a corridor. Exusiai looks in the direction of the sound—
Carrying a small bundle, the Nurturer stands in the light shining through the door. His hands and robes are stained with blood, but the bundle is clean.
With head bowed, he walks slowly toward the Hall of Enlightenment, towards the waiting Matriarch. The crowd parts to let him through.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Thank you, Andoain.
The Matriarch takes the newborn from the Nurturer. She cannot see, and thus does not realize that his brow is furrowed in sorrow.
The Matriarch gently opens the bundle, and reveals the newborn—
A fledgling beast.
He leans against the Matriarch's shoulder, mucous membrane still sticking to its infantile paws. The wet and creased fur shows no sign of relaxing.
His eyes are closed, his breathing barely audible.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: As you can see, the first life that the Shrine of Nurtury has brought into this world is this fledgling arborbeast.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: His weight is nothing. His weight is everything.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Before I came to Laterano, I found his mother in an abandoned nomadic abbey. She was so famished, her feathers fallen, that I did not at first recognize her as an arborbeast.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: A hunter's spear had impaled the mother's abdomen, but missed the fetus by inches.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I do not know how his mother hid for so long, how she survived, and how she stayed awake through the pain and hunger.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Until now.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I thank this strong mother, our Sankta and Liberi brethren, and our honored guests from afar—

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: This child was born amidst our prayers. He is a miracle that you have made together.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: But why...?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Why do his eyes not open?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Matriarch. The newborn's breathing is growing weaker...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I tried everything I could think of. His mother gave her all.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Perhaps the mother's injuries were too grave, depriving the fetus of nutrition...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Andoain, we may all have forgotten one thing.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Do you mean...?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The childbirth was long and painful. But from beginning to end, all we felt through the comfort bells, through empathy, was a single heartbeat.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This child was so weak that he could not even express his desire to live, the most primal, most instinctive cry of life.
Andoain bows his head and does not speak.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Is this what you thought the Nativity would be, Mostima?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Normally, we'd already be cutting the cake beside a crying baby...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Damn, this is depressing.

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: Do they mean that after all that effort from the mother, the baby was stillborn?

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: Che cazzo! How could this be?!

steps.name: Feline
steps.text: Lord above!

steps.name: Feline
steps.text: Is there anything we can do? Like what we did just now, the thousands of us here...

steps.name: Sankta
steps.text: What if I never felt Bailey's heartbeat after hours of waiting outside the delivery room...? What would my wife and I have done...?

steps.name: Sankta
steps.text: No, I can't bear to imagine it!

steps.name: Sankta
steps.text: Poor baby, if you can hear my voice...
Somewhere in the crowd, someone begins sobbing.
Gradually, more and more people lose control of their emotions. Their cries join together and echo through the halls, for the poor mother and her stillborn child.
Then, another cry rings out.
It is not a sad sound. It is young and bright.

The fledgling arborbeast opens its eyes, and, as though sensing the emotions of the crowd, cries out for the first time in its life. It stretches its limbs, and the sheen miraculously returns to its fur.

The Matriarch embraces the newborn life tightly, crying tears of joy. One such tear drops from the empty eye sockets behind her veil, falling upon the fledgling's head, reflecting the light of the sun.
The fledgling does not stop crying. As though driven by the wailing, the light begins to break free of the void's shackles, becoming rich and full—
A halo.
The mark of the Sankta, the symbol of the Law, the embodiment of truth. It has illuminated this unfamiliar creature—
A shining, miraculous beacon.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The Lord has once again answered our prayer. He has blessed this child.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: This is a miracle not seen in a thousand years. Its appearance on the eve of calamity is a revelation from the Law.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: We are all witnesses. We are all participants.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Henceforth, we are born equal and one, beginning with the Holy City, and ending with the Holy City.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: —As Sankta.
In the Matriarch's embrace, the newborn licks her arms. He has awakened.
Once again, the comfort bells sway. A new heartbeat, strong and regular, fills the Shrine of Nurtury.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Laterano granted a halo to an arborbeast fledgling?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Even the most incredible miracle in The Saints' Travels pales in comparison.

spans.text: Even the most incredible miracle in

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Is this a divine blessing, or a terrible calamity?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: My greater concern is whether it is true, whether it should be believed.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Since when did you start doubting everything you see?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: There are too many details, Arturia.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The unusual confessional.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The boundless wheat fields.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The crackdown on the manufacturing of firearms and explosives. The firearms workshops being shut down.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The sudden change in Landen Monastery's role.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The abrupt changes in the administration of the Curia. The colleagues who suddenly appeared to interfere with my investigation.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It was the appearance of Richele and his men, despite the fact that he should not have known my movements, that confirmed my suspicions. Otherwise, I would have continued my efforts to apprehend you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: All of these anomalies converge at this Shrine of Nurtury, which seems to have appeared out of nowhere, and the Nativity that so many have fixed their eyes on.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The missing mother you were investigating from the nomadic abbey was the pregnant arborbeast?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: By chance, my music crossed paths with the voice of her heart. I followed the trail here.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The singular item that brought me to my conclusion, of greater weight than any of the above, is how the Lateran people are seemingly oblivious to all of this.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Everything in life has been turned upside-down, but in this country, this city, life goes on, orderly as ever, as though things have always been so.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: When six million Laterans continue to live as they always have, it's hard for us to convince ourselves that we're the only sane ones.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Self-doubt is an invaluable experience for a hardhead like you, isn't it?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you certain now?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Mathematics, physics, geography, archaeology, astronomy... no theory or knowledge in science, theology, or philosophy can explain this.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A city with a population of six million, sharing the same hallucination.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But the present circumstances clearly run contrary to the order of Laterano and the foundation of the Law.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have no doubt.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What a coincidence. Neither do I—

a.text: The sound of comfort bells echoes in the sky above the city. The cello's music draws upon a crack, like a hand reaching into the city. The next instant, both sounds are brought to an abrupt halt.
The crowds that come and go in front of the square have never existed. Laterano has never been so quiet, even when the city is gazed upon from the highest roof of the Basilica.
Federico and Arturia are unsure if they blinked. A scene most incomprehensible plays out before their eyes—
The shrine continues to tower over the city, utterly out of place, but now dream-like colors begin to run across its surface.
Almost reaching the clouds, it spills its colors upon the pristine white buildings surrounding it.
Doors and windows open to the streets and alleys of Laterano, wherever the shrine's shadow touches, and creatures the likes of which have never been seen before emerge from them...
The scene is indescribable, but there is no doubt in Federico or Arturia that this is the real Laterano.
The next instant, the same word slips from their mouths.
